scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! prediction.raw:
I think you're a bit of a jerk (NTA) in this situation. While I understand that you're trying to involve your boyfriend in your son's life, your approach is a bit too pushy and demanding. You're essentially asking him to take on more responsibilities without considering his own needs and desires.

Firstly, it's not unreasonable for your boyfriend to want to spend his weekends doing things he enjoys, like watching football games. It's not like he's asking you to do something you don't want to do; he's simply expressing his own preferences.

Secondly, your boyfriend's suggestion that he's having to work longer hours to support you and your son is a valid point. You're asking him to take on more childcare responsibilities, which could impact his own work-life balance.

Lastly, your reaction to his suggestion that you break up is a bit dramatic and over-the-top. You're essentially saying, "If you don't do what I want, I'll leave you." That's not a healthy or respectful way to communicate in a relationship.

It's also worth noting that your boyfriend's dad could potentially take your son to football games, and it's not like you're being asked to do something impossible. Your boyfriend's dad might not drive, but that doesn't mean he can't find another way to get your son to the games.

Overall, I think you're being a bit too entitled and demanding in this situation. It's not about the football game itself, but about the way you're approaching your boyfriend and asking him to take on more responsibilities without considering his own needs and desires.
